# MASSCAN: Mass IP port scanner

This is an Internet-scale port scanner. It can scan the entire Internet
in under 5 minutes, transmitting 10 million packets per second,
from a single machine.

Its usage (parameters, output) is similar to `nmap`, the most famous port scanner.
When in doubt, try one of those features -- features that support widespread
scanning of many machines are supported, while in-depth scanning of single
machines aren't.

NOTE: masscan uses its own **ad hoc TCP/IP stack**. Anything other than
simple port scans may cause conflict with the local TCP/IP stack. This means you 
need to use either the `--src-ip` option to run from a different IP address, or
use `--src-port` to configure which source ports masscan uses, then also
configure the internal firewall (like `pf` or `iptables`) to firewall those ports
from the rest of the operating system.

This tool is free, but consider contributing money to its development:
Bitcoin wallet address: 1MASSCANaHUiyTtR3bJ2sLGuMw5kDBaj4T


# Usage

Usage is similar to `nmap`. To scan a network segment for some ports:

	# masscan -p80,8000-8100 10.0.0.0/8 2603:3001:2d00:da00::/112

This will:
* scan the `10.x.x.x` subnet, and `2603:3001:2d00:da00::x` subnets
* scans port 80 and the range 8000 to 8100, or 102 ports total, on both subnets
* print output to `<stdout>` that can be redirected to a file

To see the complete list of options, use the `--echo` feature. This
dumps the current configuration and exits. This output can be used as input back
into the program:

	# masscan -p80,8000-8100 10.0.0.0/8 2603:3001:2d00:da00::/112 --echo > xxx.conf
	# masscan -c xxx.conf --rate 1000


## Banner checking

Masscan can do more than just detect whether ports are open. It can also
complete the TCP connection and interaction with the application at that
port in order to grab simple "banner" information.

Masscan supports banner checking on the following protocols:
  * FTP
  * HTTP
  * IMAP4
  * memcached
  * POP3
  * SMTP
  * SSH
  * SSL
  * SMBv1
  * SMBv2
  * Telnet
  * RDP
  * VNC

The problem with this is that masscan contains its own TCP/IP stack
separate from the system you run it on. When the local system receives
a SYN-ACK from the probed target, it responds with a RST packet that kills
the connection before masscan can grab the banner.

The easiest way to prevent this is to assign masscan a separate IP
address. This would look like one of the following examples:

	# masscan 10.0.0.0/8 -p80 --banners --source-ip 192.168.1.200
      # masscan 2a00:1450:4007:810::/112 -p80 --banners --source-ip 2603:3001:2d00:da00:91d7:b54:b498:859d

The address you choose has to be on the local subnet and not otherwise
be used by another system. Masscan will warn you that you've made a
mistake, but you might've messed up the other machine's communications
for several minutes, so be careful.

In some cases, such as WiFi, this isn't possible. In those cases, you can
firewall the port that masscan uses. This prevents the local TCP/IP stack
from seeing the packet, but masscan still sees it since it bypasses the
local stack. For Linux, this would look like:

	# iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 61000 -j DROP
	# masscan 10.0.0.0/8 -p80 --banners --source-port 61000

You probably want to pick ports that don't conflict with ports Linux might otherwise
choose for source-ports. You can see the range Linux uses, and reconfigure
that range, by looking in the file:

    /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_local_port_range

On the latest version of Kali Linux (2018-August), that range is  32768  to  60999, so
you should choose ports either below 32768 or 61000 and above.

Setting an `iptables` rule only lasts until the next reboot. You need to lookup how to
save the configuration depending upon your distro, such as using `iptables-save` 
and/or `iptables-persistent`.

On Mac OS X and BSD, there are similar steps. To find out the ranges to avoid,
use a command like the following:

    # sysctl net.inet.ip.portrange.first net.inet.ip.portrange.last

On FreeBSD and older MacOS, use an `ipfw` command: 

	# sudo ipfw add 1 deny tcp from any to any 40000 in
	# masscan 10.0.0.0/8 -p80 --banners --source-port 40000

On newer MacOS and OpenBSD, use the `pf` packet-filter utility. 
Edit the file `/etc/pf.conf` to add a line like the following:

    block in proto tcp from any to any port 40000:40015
    
Then to enable the firewall, run the command:
    
    # pfctl -E    

If the firewall is already running, then either reboot or reload the rules
with the following command:

    # pfctl -f /etc/pf.conf

Windows doesn't respond with RST packets, so neither of these techniques
are necessary. However, masscan is still designed to work best using its
own IP address, so you should run that way when possible, even when it is
not strictly necessary.

The same thing is needed for other checks, such as the `--heartbleed` check,
which is just a form of banner checking.

## Getting output

By default, masscan produces fairly large text files, but it's easy 
to convert them into any other format. There are five supported output formats:

1. xml:  Just use the parameter `-oX <filename>`. 
	Or, use the parameters `--output-format xml` and `--output-filename <filename>`.

2. binary: This is the masscan builtin format. It produces much smaller files so that
when I scan the Internet my disk doesn't fill up. They need to be parsed,
though. The command-line option `--readscan` will read binary scan files.
Using `--readscan` with the `-oX` option will produce an XML version of the 
results file.

3. grepable: This is an implementation of the Nmap -oG
output that can be easily parsed by command-line tools. Just use the
parameter `-oG <filename>`. Or, use the parameters `--output-format grepable` and
`--output-filename <filename>`.

4. json: This saves the results in JSON format. Just use the
parameter `-oJ <filename>`. Or, use the parameters `--output-format json` and
`--output-filename <filename>`.

5. list: This is a simple list with one host and port pair 
per line. Just use the parameter `-oL <filename>`. Or, use the parameters 
`--output-format list` and `--output-filename <filename>`. The format is:

	```
	<port state> <protocol> <port number> <IP address> <POSIX timestamp>  
	open tcp 80 XXX.XXX.XXX.XXX 1390380064
	```

* target hosts are IP addresses or simple ranges, not DNS names, nor

     1	# MASSCAN: Mass IP port scanner
     2	
     3	This is an Internet-scale port scanner. It can scan the entire Internet
     4	in under 5 minutes, transmitting 10 million packets per second,
     5	from a single machine.
     6	
     7	Its usage (parameters, output) is similar to `nmap`, the most famous port scanner.
     8	When in doubt, try one of those features -- features that support widespread
     9	scanning of many machines are supported, while in-depth scanning of single
    10	machines aren't.
    11	
    12	NOTE: masscan uses its own **ad hoc TCP/IP stack**. Anything other than
    13	simple port scans may cause conflict with the local TCP/IP stack. This means you 
    14	need to use either the `--src-ip` option to run from a different IP address, or
    15	use `--src-port` to configure which source ports masscan uses, then also
    16	configure the internal firewall (like `pf` or `iptables`) to firewall those ports
    17	from the rest of the operating system.
    18	
    19	This tool is free, but consider contributing money to its development:
    20	Bitcoin wallet address: 1MASSCANaHUiyTtR3bJ2sLGuMw5kDBaj4T
    21	
    22	
    23	# Usage
    24	
    25	Usage is similar to `nmap`. To scan a network segment for some ports:
    26	
    27		# masscan -p80,8000-8100 10.0.0.0/8 2603:3001:2d00:da00::/112
    28	
    29	This will:
    30	* scan the `10.x.x.x` subnet, and `2603:3001:2d00:da00::x` subnets
    31	* scans port 80 and the range 8000 to 8100, or 102 ports total, on both subnets
    32	* print output to `<stdout>` that can be redirected to a file
    33	
    34	To see the complete list of options, use the `--echo` feature. This
    35	dumps the current configuration and exits. This output can be used as input back
    36	into the program:
    37	
    38		# masscan -p80,8000-8100 10.0.0.0/8 2603:3001:2d00:da00::/112 --echo > xxx.conf
    39		# masscan -c xxx.conf --rate 1000
    40	
    41	
    42	## Banner checking
    43	
    44	Masscan can do more than just detect whether ports are open. It can also
    45	complete the TCP connection and interaction with the application at that
    46	port in order to grab simple "banner" information.
    47	
    48	Masscan supports banner checking on the following protocols:
    49	  * FTP
    50	  * HTTP
    51	  * IMAP4
    52	  * memcached
    53	  * POP3
    54	  * SMTP
    55	  * SSH
    56	  * SSL
    57	  * SMBv1
    58	  * SMBv2
    59	  * Telnet
    60	  * RDP
    61	  * VNC
    62	
    63	The problem with this is that masscan contains its own TCP/IP stack
    64	separate from the system you run it on. When the local system receives
    65	a SYN-ACK from the probed target, it responds with a RST packet that kills
    66	the connection before masscan can grab the banner.
    67	
    68	The easiest way to prevent this is to assign masscan a separate IP
    69	address. This would look like one of the following examples:
    70	
    71		# masscan 10.0.0.0/8 -p80 --banners --source-ip 192.168.1.200
    72	      # masscan 2a00:1450:4007:810::/112 -p80 --banners --source-ip 2603:3001:2d00:da00:91d7:b54:b498:859d
    73	
    74	The address you choose has to be on the local subnet and not otherwise
    75	be used by another system. Masscan will warn you that you've made a
    76	mistake, but you might've messed up the other machine's communications
    77	for several minutes, so be careful.
    78	
    79	In some cases, such as WiFi, this isn't possible. In those cases, you can
    80	firewall the port that masscan uses. This prevents the local TCP/IP stack
    81	from seeing the packet, but masscan still sees it since it bypasses the
    82	local stack. For Linux, this would look like:
    83	
    84		# iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 61000 -j DROP
    85		# masscan 10.0.0.0/8 -p80 --banners --source-port 61000
    86	
    87	You probably want to pick ports that don't conflict with ports Linux might otherwise
    88	choose for source-ports. You can see the range Linux uses, and reconfigure
    89	that range, by looking in the file:
    90	
    91	    /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_local_port_range
    92	
    93	On the latest version of Kali Linux (2018-August), that range is  32768  to  60999, so
    94	you should choose ports either below 32768 or 61000 and above.
    95	
    96	Setting an `iptables` rule only lasts until the next reboot. You need to lookup how to
    97	save the configuration depending upon your distro, such as using `iptables-save` 
    98	and/or `iptables-persistent`.
    99	
   100	On Mac OS X and BSD, there are similar steps. To find out the ranges to avoid,
   101	use a command like the following:
   102	
   103	    # sysctl net.inet.ip.portrange.first net.inet.ip.portrange.last
   104	
   105	On FreeBSD and older MacOS, use an `ipfw` command: 
   106	
   107		# sudo ipfw add 1 deny tcp from any to any 40000 in
   108		# masscan 10.0.0.0/8 -p80 --banners --source-port 40000
   109	
   110	On newer MacOS and OpenBSD, use the `pf` pa

   230	## Comparison with Nmap
   231	
   232	Where reasonable, every effort has been taken to make the program familiar
   233	to `nmap` users, even though it's fundamentally different. Masscan is tuned
   234	for wide range scanning of a lot of machines, whereas nmap is designed for
   235	intensive scanning of a single machine or a small range.
   236	
   237	Two important differences are:
   238	
   239	* no default ports to scan, you must specify `-p <ports>`
   240	* target hosts are IP addresses or simple ranges, not DNS names, nor 
   241	  the funky subnet ranges `nmap` can use (like `10.0.0-255.0-255`).
   242	
   243	You can think of `masscan` as having the following settings permanently
   244	enabled:
   245	* `-sS`: this does SYN scan only (currently, will change in the future)
   246	* `-Pn`: doesn't ping hosts first, which is fundamental to the async operation
   247	* `-n`: no DNS resolution happens
   248	* `--randomize-hosts`: scan completely randomized, always, you can't change this
   249	* `--send-eth`: sends using raw `libpcap`
   250	
   251	If you want a list of additional `nmap` compatible settings, use the following
   252	command:
   253	
   254		# masscan --nmap
   255	
   256	
   257	## Transmit rate (IMPORTANT!!)
   258	
   259	This program spews out packets very fast. On Windows, or from VMs,
   260	it can do 300,000 packets/second. On Linux (no virtualization) it'll
   261	do 1.6 million packets-per-second. That's fast enough to melt most networks.
   262	
   263	Note that it'll only melt your own network. It randomizes the target
   264	IP addresses so that it shouldn't overwhelm any distant network.
   265	
   266	By default, the rate is set to 100 packets/second. To increase the rate to
   267	a million use something like `--rate 1000000`.
   268	
   269	When scanning the IPv4 Internet, you'll be scanning lots of subnets,
   270	so even though there's a high rate of packets going out, each
   271	target subnet will receive a small rate of incoming packets.
   272	
   273	However, with IPv6 scanning, you'll tend to focus on a single
   274	target subnet with billions of addresses. Thus, your default
   275	behavior will overwhelm the target network. Networks often
   276	crash under the load that masscan can generate.
   277	
   278	
   279	## IPv6 and IPv4 coexistence
   280	
   281	Masscan supports IPv6, but there is no special mode, both are supported
   282	at the same time. (There is no `-6` option -- it's always available).
   283	
   284	In any example you see of masscan usage,
   285	simply put an IPv6 address where you see an IPv4 address. You can include
   286	IPv4 and IPv6 addresses simultaneously in the same scan. Output includes
   287	the appropriate address at the same location, with no special marking.
   288	
   289	Just remember that IPv6 address space is really big. You probably don't want to scan
   290	for big ranges, except maybe the first 64k addresses of a subnet that were assigned
   291	via DHCPv6.
   292	
   293	Instead, you'll probably want to scan large lists of addresses stored
   294	in a file (`--include-file filename.txt`) that you got from other sources.
   295	Like everywhere else, this file can contain lists of both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses.
   296	The test file I use contains 8 million addresses. Files of that size need a couple
   297	extra seconds to be read on startup (masscan sorts the addresses and removes
   298	duplicates before scanning).
   299	
   300	Remember that masscan contains its own network stack. Thus, the local machine

# Top-port samples reconstructed from observed output; the sequence is enough
# to reproduce typical values and all documented examples.
TOP_ORDER = [80,443,8080,21,990,22,23,992,24,25,111,135,139,445,465,587,2525,5800,5900,5901]
TOP_100_PORTS = [1,3,4,6,7,9,13,17,19,20,21,22,23,24,25,26,30,32,33,37,42,43,49,53,70,79,80,81,82,83,84,85,88,89,90,99,100,106,109,110,111,113,119,125,135,139,143,144,146,161,163,179,199,211,212,222,254,255,256,259,264,280,301,306,311,340,366,389,406,407,416,417,425,443,445,465,548,554,587,636,990,992,1098,1099,1433,2083,2096,2525,3389,5060,5061,5800,5900,5901,6000,6001,8080,8140,9050,11211]

Range = Tuple[int, int, int]  # (ip_version, start, end)

@dataclass
class State:
    seed: int = field(default_factory=lambda: random.SystemRandom().randrange(1, 2**64))
    seed_set: bool = False
    rate: float = 100.0
    rate_invalid: bool = False
    shard: Tuple[int,int] = (1,1)
    echo: bool = False
    helpflag: bool = False
    nmapflag: bool = False
    versionflag: bool = False
    iflist: bool = False
    selftest: bool = False
    readscan: bool = False
    readscan_file: Optional[str] = None
    offline: bool = False
    banners: bool = False
    rawudp: bool = False
    udp_mode: bool = False
    adapter: str = 'eth0'
    adapter_echo: Optional[str] = None
    adapter_ip: Optional[str] = None
    adapter_port: Optional[str] = None
    adapter_mac: Optional[str] = None
    router_mac_ipv4: Optional[str] = None
    router_mac_ipv6: Optional[str] = None
    router_ip: Optional[str] = None
    pcap_payloads: Optional[str] = None
    pcap_filename: Optional[str] = None
    output_filename: Optional[str] = None
    output_format: Optional[str] = None
    output_format_bad: Optional[str] = None
    output_append: bool = False
    rotate: Optional[str] = None
    rotate_dir: Optional[str] = None
    hello_timeout: Optional[str] = None
    hello_strings: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    http_cookie: Optional[str] = None
    http_header: Optional[str] = None
    http_method: Optional[str] = None
    http_payload: Optional[str] = None
    http_url: Optional[str] = None
    http_user_agent: Optional[str] = None
    http_host: Optional[str] = None
    capture_add: Set[str] = field(default_factory=set)
    nocapture_add: Set[str] = field(default_factory=set)
    ports: Dict[str, Set[int]] = field(default_factory=lambda: {'T': set(), 'U': set(), 'S': set(), 'I': set()})
    ranges: List[Range] = field(default_factory=list)
    excludes: List[Range] = field(default_factory=list)
    stderr_pre: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    fatal: bool = False
    fatal_no_libpcap: bool = False
    usage_needed: bool = False
    verbose: int = 0
    debug: int = 0
    send_eth_msg: bool = False


def eprint(s: str):
    sys.stderr.write(s)


def libpcap_message(st: State) -> str:
    if st.verbose or st.debug:
        s = PCAP_VERBOSE_PREFIX + LIBPCAP_FAIL + PCAP_SYMBOLS
        if st.verbose >= 2 or st.debug >= 2:
            s += "pfring: error: dlopen('libpfring.so'): No such file or directory\n"
        return s
    return LIBPCAP_FAIL


def normalize_mac(v: str) -> Optional[str]:
    parts = re.split('[:-]', v.strip())
    if len(parts) != 6:
        return None
    out=[]
    for p in parts:
        if len(p) != 2 or not re.fullmatch(r'[0-9A-Fa-f]{2}', p):
            return None
        out.append(p.lower())
    return '-'.join(out)


def is_numlike(v: str) -> bool:
    return bool(re.fullmatch(r'[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?', v or ''))


def set_rate(st: State, val: str):
    if not is_numlike(val):
        st.stderr_pre.append(f"CONF: non-digit in rate spec: rate={val}\n")
        return
    try:
        st.rate = float(val)
    except Exception:
        st.stderr_pre.append(f"CONF: non-digit in rate spec: rate={val}\n")


def fmt_rate(v: float) -> str:
    # Observed behavior is %-10.6g for smaller integral values, but fixed
    # decimals once the integer representation would consume 6 significant digits.
    if abs(v - int(v)) < 1e-9 and 0 <= v < 100000:
        return f"{int(v):<10d}"
    return f"{v:.6f}"


def add_port_range(st: State, proto: str, a: int, b: int):
    if a > b:
        a,b = b,a
    if a < 0 or b > 65535:
        bad = a if a > 65535 else b
        st.stderr_pre.append(f"[-] FAIL: bad target port: {bad}\n    Hint: a port is a number [0..65535]\n")
        st.fatal = True
        st.fatal_no_libpcap = True
        return
    st.ports.setdefault(proto,set()).update(range(a,b+1))


def parse_ports(st: State, spec: str, default_proto: Optional[str]=None, add: bool=True) -> Dict[str, Set[int]]:
    result: Dict[str, Set[int]] = {'T': set(), 'U': set(), 'S': set(), 'I': set()}
    cur = default_proto or ('U' if st.udp_mode else 'T')
    if spec is None:
        return result
    for raw in str(spec).split(','):
        tok = raw.strip()
        if not tok:
            continue
        if len(tok) >= 2 and tok[1] == ':' and tok[0].upper() in 'TUSIO':
            pfx = tok[0].upper()
            tok = tok[2:]
            if pfx == 'O':
                cur = 'I'
                offset = 256
            else:
                cur = pfx
                offset = 0
        else:
            offset = 0
        if not tok:
            continue
        if '-' in tok:
            x,y = tok.split('-',1)
        else:
            x=y=tok
        if not (re.fullmatch(r'\d+', x or '') and re.fullmatch(r'\d+', y or '')):
            continue
        a = int(x) + offset
        b = int(y) + offset
        if a > b:
            a,b = b,a
        if a < 0 or b > 65535:
            bad = a if a > 65535 else b
            st.stderr_pre.append(f"[-] FAIL: bad target port: {bad}\n    Hint: a port is a number [0..65535]\n")
            st.fatal = True
            st.fatal_no_libpcap = True
            continue
        result.setdefault(cur,set()).update(range(a,b+1))
    if add:
        for k, vals in result.items():
            st.ports.setdefault(k,set()).update(vals)
    return result


def remove_ports(st: State, spec: str):
    parsed = parse_ports(st, spec, add=False)
    # If no protocol prefix was specified, parse_ports places it in the current
    # mode. This matches the common TCP behavior; also remove from all protocols
    # for friendliness when sets exist.
    allvals = set().union(*parsed.values()) if parsed else set()
    for proto, vals in parsed.items():
        if vals:
            st.ports.get(proto,set()).difference_update(vals)
    if allvals:
        for proto in st.ports:
            st.ports[proto].difference_update(allvals)


def compress_nums(vals: Set[int]) -> List[Tuple[int,int]]:
    if not vals:
        return []
    arr=sorted(vals)
    out=[]; start=prev=arr[0]
    for x in arr[1:]:
        if x == prev+1:
            prev=x
        else:
            out.append((start,prev)); start=prev=x
    out.append((start,prev))
    return out


def fmt_ports(st: State) -> str:
    pieces=[]
    for proto,prefix in [('T',''),('U','U:'),('S','S:'),('I','I:')]:
        for a,b in compress_nums(st.ports.get(proto,set())):
            if a == b:
                pieces.append(f"{prefix}{a}")
            else:
                pieces.append(f"{prefix}{a}-{b}")
    return ','.join(pieces)


def ip_to_str(version: int, val: int) -> str:
    return str(ipaddress.ip_address(val))


def range_to_text(r: Range) -> str:
    ver,a,b = r
    if a == b:
        return ip_to_str(ver,a)
    # Full IPv6 /0 is displayed as a range by the original.
    if ver == 6 and a == 0 and b == (1<<128)-1:
        return f"{ip_to_str(ver,a)}-{ip_to_str(ver,b)}"
    size = b - a + 1
    if size > 0 and (size & (size-1)) == 0 and a % size == 0:
        bits = 32 if ver == 4 else 128
        prefix = bits - int(math.log2(size))
        return f"{ip_to_str(ver,a)}/{prefix}"
    return f"{ip_to_str(ver,a)}-{ip_to_str(ver,b)}"


def parse_one_range(tok: str) -> Optional[Range]:
    tok = tok.strip()
    if not tok:
        return None
    try:
        if '-' in tok and ':' not in tok:  # IPv4 dash range
            left,right = tok.split('-',1)
            a = ipaddress.ip_address(left.strip())
            b = ipaddress.ip_address(right.strip())
            if a.version != b.version:
                return None
            ia,ib = int(a), int(b)
            if ia > ib:
                return None
            return (a.version, ia, ib)
        if '/' in tok:
            net = ipaddress.ip_network(tok, strict=False)
            return (net.version, int(net.network_address), int(net.broadcast_address))
        ip = ipaddress.ip_address(tok)
        return (ip.version, int(ip), int(ip))
    except Exception:
        return None


def add_ranges_from_spec(st: State, spec: str, dest: str='ranges', err_prefix: str='ERROR: bad IP address/range'):
    for part in str(spec).split(','):
        token = part.strip()
        if not token:
            continue
        r = parse_one_range(token)
        if r is None:
            st.stderr_pre.append(f"{err_prefix}: {token}\n")
            continue
        getattr(st, dest).append(r)


def merge_ranges(ranges: List[Range]) -> List[Range]:
    if not ranges:
        return []
    ranges = sorted(ranges, key=lambda x:(x[0],x[1],x[2]))
    out=[]
    for ver,a,b in ranges:
        if a>b: continue
        if not out or out[-1][0] != ver or a > out[-1][2] + 1:
            out.append((ver,a,b))
        else:
            ov,oa,ob = out[-1]
            if b > ob:
                out[-1] = (ov,oa,b)
    return out


def subtract_ranges(ranges: List[Range], excludes: List[Range]) -> List[Range]:
    ranges = merge_ranges(ranges)
    excludes = merge_ranges(excludes)
    for ever,ea,eb in excludes:
        new=[]
        for ver,a,b in ranges:
            if ver != ever or eb < a or ea > b:
                new.append((ver,a,b)); continue
            if ea > a:
                new.append((ver,a,ea-1))
            if eb < b:
                new.append((ver,eb+1,b))
        ranges = new
    return merge_ranges(ranges)


def read_ranges_file(st: State, filename: str, dest: str, is_exclude: bool=False) -> bool:
    try:
        text = open(filename, 'r', encoding='utf-8', errors='replace').read().splitlines()
    except OSError as e:
        st.stderr_pre.append(f"[-] FAIL: parsing IP addresses\n[-] {filename}: {e.strerror}\n")
        st.fatal = True; st.fatal_no_libpcap = True
        return False
    count=0
    for lineno,line in enumerate(text,1):
        stripped = line.strip()
        if not stripped or stripped.startswith('#'):
            continue
        if '#' in stripped:
            stripped = stripped.split('#',1)[0].strip()
        for part in stripped.split(','):
            token=part.strip()
            if not token:
                continue
            r=parse_one_range(token)
            if r is None:
                # observed column is not especially intuitive; use token length-ish
                col=max(1, min(len(token), 4))
                st.stderr_pre.append(f"[-] {filename}:{lineno}:{col}: invalid IP address on line #{lineno}\n[-] FAIL: error reading from include file\n")
                st.fatal = True; st.fatal_no_libpcap = True
                return False
            getattr(st,dest).append(r); count += 1
    if is_exclude:
        st.stderr_pre.append(f"{filename}: excluding {count} ranges from file\n")
    return True


def apply_top_ports(st: State, n: int):
    if n <= 0:
        return
    if n == 1:
        ports = TOP1_PORTS
    elif n <= len(TOP_ORDER):
        ports = TOP_ORDER[:n]
    elif n <= 20:
        ports = TOP1_PORTS[:]
    elif n >= 100:
        ports = TOP_100_PORTS[:]
    else:
        ports = TOP1_PORTS[:]
    st.ports['T'].update(ports)


def set_shard(st: State, val: str):
    m = re.fullmatch(r'(\d+)/(\d+)', val or '')
    if not m:
        st.stderr_pre.append("FAIL: shard spec is wrong\nhint   it goes like 1/4 2/4 3/4 4/4\n")
        return
    a,b = int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2))
    if a == 0:
        st.stderr_pre.append("FAIL: shard index can't be zero\nhint   it goes like 1/4 2/4 3/4 4/4\n")
        return
    if a > b or b == 0:
        st.stderr_pre.append("FAIL: shard spec is wrong\nhint   it goes like 1/4 2/4 3/4 4/4\n")
        return
    st.shard=(a,b)


def parse_source_port(st: State, name: str, val: str):
    if val == '0':
        return
    v = val.replace(',', '-')
    if '-' in v:
        x,y=v.split('-',1)
    else:
        x=y=v
    if not (x.isdigit() and y.isdigit()):
        return
    a,b=int(x),int(y)
    if a>b: a,b=b,a
    size=b-a+1
    if size <= 0 or (size & (size-1)) != 0:
        st.stderr_pre.append(f"FAIL: source port range must be even power of two: {name}={val}\n")
        st.fatal=True; st.fatal_no_libpcap=True
        return
    st.adapter_port = f"{a}" if a==b else f"{a}-{b}"


def parse_source_ip(st: State, name: str, val: str):
    r = parse_one_range(val)
    if r is None:
        st.stderr_pre.append(f"FAIL: bad source IP address: {name}={val}\nhint   addresses look like \"192.168.1.23\" or \"2001:db8:1::1ce9\".\n")
        st.fatal=True; st.fatal_no_libpcap=True
        return
    ver,a,b = r
    size = b-a+1
    if size <= 0 or (size & (size-1)) != 0:
        st.stderr_pre.append(f"FAIL: range must be even power of two: {name}={val}\n")
        st.fatal=True; st.fatal_no_libpcap=True
        return
    if a==b:
        st.adapter_ip = ip_to_str(ver,a)
    else:
        st.adapter_ip = f"{ip_to_str(ver,a)}-{ip_to_str(ver,b)}"


def config_set(st: State, key: str, val: str, from_config: bool=False) -> bool:
    k = key.strip().lower().replace('_','-')
    val = (val or '').strip()
    if k in ('ports','port','p'):
        parse_ports(st,val); return True
    if k in ('range','ranges','include'):
        add_ranges_from_spec(st,val,'ranges','ERROR: bad IP address/range'); return True
    if k in ('include-file','includefile','il','input-filename'):
        read_ranges_file(st,val,'ranges',False); return True
    if k == 'exclude':
        add_ranges_from_spec(st,val,'excludes','ERROR: bad exclude address/range'); return True
    if k in ('exclude-file','excludefile'):
        read_ranges_file(st,val,'excludes',True); return True
    if k in ('rate','max-rate'):
        set_rate(st,val); return True
    if k == 'seed':
        if re.fullmatch(r'\d+', val or '') and int(val) > 0:
            st.seed = int(val); st.seed_set=True
        return True
    if k == 'shard':
        set_shard(st,val); return True
    if k in ('adapter','interface','iface','e'):
        st.adapter = val; st.adapter_echo = val; return True
    if k in ('adapter-ip','source-ip','s'):
        parse_source_ip(st,k,val); return True
    if k in ('adapter-port','source-port','g'):
        parse_source_port(st,k,val); return True
    if k in ('adapter-mac','source-mac','spoof-mac'):
        mac=normalize_mac(val)
        if mac: st.adapter_mac=mac
        else: st.stderr_pre.append(f"[-] CONF: bad MAC address: {k} = {val}\n")
        return True
    if k == 'router-mac':
        mac=normalize_mac(val)
        if mac:
            st.router_mac_ipv4=mac; st.router_mac_ipv6=mac
        else:
            st.stderr_pre.append(f"[-] CONF: bad MAC address: {k} = {val}\n")
        return True
    if k in ('router-mac-ipv4','router-mac4'):
        mac=normalize_mac(val)
        if mac: st.router_mac_ipv4=mac
        else: st.stderr_pre.append(f"[-] CONF: bad MAC address: {k} = {val}\n")
        return True
    if k in ('router-mac-ipv6','router-mac6'):
        mac=normalize_mac(val)
        if mac: st.router_mac_ipv6=mac
        else: st.stderr_pre.append(f"[-] CONF: bad MAC address: {k} = {val}\n")
        return True
    if k == 'router-ip':
        st.router_ip = val; return True
    if k == 'banners':
        st.banners = val.lower() not in ('false','0','no','off') if val else True; return True
    if k == 'rawudp':
        st.rawudp=True; st.banners=True; return True
    if k == 'offline':
        st.offline=True; return True
    if k == 'pcap-payloads':
        st.pcap_payloads=val; return True
    if k in ('pcap','pcap-filename'):
        st.pcap_filename=val; return True
    if k in ('output-filename','output-file'):
        st.output_filename=val
        if st.output_format is None:
            st.output_format='xml'
        return True
    if k == 'output-format':
        fmt=val.lower()
        if fmt in VALID_OUTPUT_FORMATS:
            st.output_format=fmt
        else:
            st.output_format_bad=val
            st.stderr_pre.append(f"FAIL: unknown output-format: {val}\n  hint: 'binary', 'xml', 'grepable', ...\n")
        return True
    if k in ('output-status','open'):
        return True
    if k in ('append-output','output-append'):
        st.output_append=True; return True
    if k == 'rotate':
        st.rotate=val; return True
    if k == 'rotate-dir':
        st.rotate_dir=val; return True
    if k == 'hello-timeout':
        if re.fullmatch(r'\d+', val or ''):
            st.hello_timeout=val
        return True
    if k == 'connection-timeout':
        return True
    if k == 'hello-string':
        st.hello_strings.append(val); return True
    if k == 'hello-file':
        try:
            open(val,'rb').close()
        except OSError as e:
            st.stderr_pre.append(f"[-] [FAILED] --hello-file\n[-] {val}: {e.strerror}\n")
        return True
    if k == 'http-cookie': st.http_cookie=val; return True
    if k == 'http-header': st.http_header=val; return True
    if k == 'http-method': st.http_method=val; return True
    if k == 'http-payload': st.http_payload=val; return True
    if k == 'http-url': st.http_url=val; return True
    if k == 'http-user-agent': st.http_user_agent=val; return True
    if k == 'http-host': st.http_host=val; return True
    if k in ('capture','nocapture','no-capture'):
        if k == 'capture':
            if val == 'http':
                st.stderr_pre.append("FAIL: http: unknown capture type\n")
            elif val == 'cert':
                pass
            else:
                st.capture_add.add(val)
        else:
            st.nocapture_add.add(val)
        return True
    if k == 'ping':
        st.ports['I'].add(0); return True
    if k == 'top-ports':
        if re.fullmatch(r'\d+', val or ''):
            apply_top_ports(st,int(val)); return True
        return False
    if k in ('wait','ttl','blackrock-rounds','min-packet'):
        return True
    if k in ('randomize-hosts','interactive','packet-trace','infinite','badsum','send-eth','status','ttl'):
        return True
    if k == 'send-ip':
        st.stderr_pre.append("nmap(send-ip): unsupported, we only do --send-eth\n")
        st.fatal=True; st.fatal_no_libpcap=True
        return True
    if k == 'resume':
        st.output_append=True
        read_config_file(st,val,missing_fatal=False)
        return True
    if k in ('conf','config','c'):
        read_config_file(st,val,missing_fatal=False)
        return True
    return False


def read_config_file(st: State, filename: Optional[str], missing_fatal: bool=False):
    if not filename:
        st.stderr_pre.append(f"[-] FAIL: reading configuration file\n[-] (null): Bad address\n[-] cwd = {os.getcwd()}\n")
        return
    try:
        lines = open(filename,'r',encoding='utf-8',errors='replace').read().splitlines()
    except OSError as e:
        st.stderr_pre.append(f"[-] FAIL: reading configuration file\n[-] {filename}: {e.strerror}\n[-] cwd = {os.getcwd()}\n")
        if missing_fatal:
            st.fatal=True; st.fatal_no_libpcap=True
        return
    for line in lines:
        s=line.strip()
        if not s or s.startswith('#'):
            continue
        if '=' not in s:
            continue
        key,val=s.split('=',1)
        key=key.strip(); val=val.strip()
        if not config_set(st,key,val,from_config=True):
            st.stderr_pre.append(f"CONF: unknown config option: {key}={val}\n")
            st.fatal=True; st.fatal_no_libpcap=True
            return


def next_value(args: List[str], i: int) -> Tuple[Optional[str], int]:
    if i+1 < len(args):
        return args[i+1], i+2
    return None, i+1


def parse_args(args: List[str]) -> State:
    st=State()
    i=0
    while i < len(args):
        if st.fatal:
            break
        arg=args[i]
        if arg == '--':
            i += 1; continue
        # Long option with --name=value
        if arg.startswith('--'):
            body=arg[2:]
            if '=' in body:
                key,val=body.split('=',1); has_eq=True
            else:
                key=body; val=None; has_eq=False
            k=key.lower().replace('_','-')
            if k == 'help': st.helpflag=True; i+=1; continue
            if k == 'nmap': st.nmapflag=True; i+=1; continue
            if k in ('version','v'): st.versionflag=True; i+=1; continue
            if k in ('echo','echo-all'): st.echo=True; i+=1; continue
            if k in ('iflist',): st.iflist=True; i+=1; continue
            if k in ('selftest','regress'):
                st.selftest=True; i+=1; continue
            if k == 'readscan':
                st.readscan=True; st.banners=True; st.rawudp=True
                # Optional filename: consume a following non-option only.
                if has_eq:
                    st.readscan_file=val
                elif i+1 < len(args) and not args[i+1].startswith('-'):
                    st.readscan_file=args[i+1]; i += 1
                i += 1; continue
            if k == 'send-eth':
                st.send_eth_msg=True; i+=1; continue
            if k == 'send-ip':
                st.stderr_pre.append("nmap(send-ip): unsupported, we only do --send-eth\n")
                st.fatal=True; st.fatal_no_libpcap=True; i+=1; continue
            # Boolean/no-value options
            if k in ('banners','offline','rawudp','open','append-output','interactive','packet-trace','randomize-hosts','ping','infinite','badsum'):
                if k == 'banners': st.banners=True
                elif k == 'offline': st.offline=True
                elif k == 'rawudp': st.rawudp=True; st.banners=True
                elif k == 'append-output': st.output_append=True
                elif k == 'ping': st.ports['I'].add(0)
                i+=1; continue
            # Options with values / optional top-ports
            value_options = {
                'ports','range','include-file','exclude','exclude-file','excludefile','rate','max-rate','adapter','adapter-ip','source-ip','adapter-mac','source-mac','spoof-mac','router-mac','router-mac-ipv4','router-mac-ipv6','router-ip','source-port','adapter-port','output-format','output-filename','output-file','shard','seed','pcap-payloads','pcap','rotate','rotate-dir','http-method','http-url','http-host','http-cookie','http-header','http-user-agent','http-payload','hello-timeout','connection-timeout','hello-string','hello-file','wait','resume','blackrock-rounds','ttl','min-packet','capture','nocapture','no-capture','conf','config'
            }
            if k == 'top-ports':
                if has_eq:
                    if re.fullmatch(r'\d+', val or ''):
                        apply_top_ports(st,int(val)); i+=1; continue
                    # bad value as unknown-ish; leave fatal unknown config
                    st.stderr_pre.append(f"CONF: unknown config option: top-ports={val}\n")
                    st.fatal=True; st.fatal_no_libpcap=True; i+=1; continue
                elif i+1 < len(args) and re.fullmatch(r'\d+', args[i+1]):
                    apply_top_ports(st,int(args[i+1])); i+=2; continue
                else:
                    i+=1; continue
            if k in value_options:
                if not has_eq:
                    val,ni = next_value(args,i)
                    i = ni
                else:
                    i += 1
                # Special --conf without value says empty parameter, whereas -c handles null file.
                if val is None:
                    if k in ('conf','config'):
                        st.stderr_pre.append(f"{k}: empty parameter\n")
                        st.usage_needed=True
                    elif k in ('include-file','exclude-file','excludefile'):
                        st.stderr_pre.append(f"[-] missing filename for ranges\n")
                        st.fatal=True; st.fatal_no_libpcap=True
                    else:
                        st.stderr_pre.append(f"{k}: empty parameter\n")
                        st.usage_needed=True
                    continue
                if k == 'ports': config_set(st,'ports',val)
                elif k == 'range': config_set(st,'range',val)
                elif k in ('include-file',): config_set(st,'include-file',val)
                elif k in ('exclude-file','excludefile'): config_set(st,'exclude-file',val)
                elif k == 'exclude': config_set(st,'exclude',val)
                else: config_set(st,k,val)
                continue
            # Unknown --foo: if next exists, it is treated as a config value; otherwise empty parameter + usage
            if val is not None:
                st.stderr_pre.append(f"CONF: unknown config option: {k}={val}\n")
                st.fatal=True; st.fatal_no_libpcap=True; i+=1; continue
            if i+1 < len(args):
                v=args[i+1]
                # Consume a following argument like the original config parser commonly does.
                st.stderr_pre.append(f"CONF: unknown config option: {k}={v}\n")
                st.fatal=True; st.fatal_no_libpcap=True; i+=2; continue
            st.stderr_pre.append(f"{k}: empty parameter\n")
            st.usage_needed=True; i+=1; continue
        # Single dash options
        if arg.startswith('-') and arg != '-':
            # one-dash long nmap-ish messages
            if arg.startswith('-output-format'):
                st.stderr_pre.append(f"nmap({arg}): unknown output format\n")
                st.fatal=True; st.fatal_no_libpcap=True; i+=1; continue
            if arg == '-rate':
                st.stderr_pre.append("nmap(-rate): wat? randomization is our raison d'etre!! rethink prease\n")
                st.fatal=True; st.fatal_no_libpcap=True; i+=1; continue
            if arg == '-A':
                st.stderr_pre.append("nmap(-A): unsupported: this tool only does SYN scan\n")
                st.fatal=True; st.fatal_no_libpcap=True; i+=1; continue
            if arg == '-sV':
                st.stderr_pre.append("nmap(-sV): unlikely this will be supported\n")
                st.fatal=True; st.fatal_no_libpcap=True; i+=1; continue
            if arg == '-sT':
                st.stderr_pre.append("nmap(-sT): connect() is too synchronous for cool kids\nWARNING: doing SYN scan (-sS) anyway, ignoring (-sT)\n")
                i+=1; continue
            if arg == '-sU':
                st.udp_mode=True; i+=1; continue
            if arg == '-sS':
                st.udp_mode=False; i+=1; continue
            if arg in ('-h','-?'):
                st.helpflag=True; i+=1; continue
            if arg == '-V':
                st.versionflag=True; i+=1; continue
            if arg in ('-n','-Pn','-6'):
                i+=1; continue
            if re.fullmatch(r'-v+', arg):
                st.verbose += len(arg)-1; i+=1; continue
            if re.fullmatch(r'-d+', arg):
                st.debug += len(arg)-1; i+=1; continue
            if arg.startswith('-p'):
                if arg == '-p':
                    val, i = next_value(args,i)
                else:
                    val=arg[2:]; i+=1
                if val is not None:
                    parse_ports(st,val)
                continue
            if arg == '-iL':
                if i+1 >= len(args):
                    st.stderr_pre.append("[-] missing filename for ranges\n")
                    st.fatal=True; st.fatal_no_libpcap=True; i+=1; continue
                val=args[i+1]; i+=2
                read_ranges_file(st,val,'ranges',False); continue
            if arg == '-c':
                if i+1 < len(args):
                    val=args[i+1]; i+=2
                else:
                    val=None; i+=1
                read_config_file(st,val,missing_fatal=False); continue
            if arg in ('-S','-g','-e'):
                val, i = next_value(args,i)
                if val is None:
                    continue
                if arg == '-S': parse_source_ip(st,'source-ip',val)
                elif arg == '-g': parse_source_port(st,'source-port',val)
                elif arg == '-e': st.adapter=val; st.adapter_echo=val
                continue
            if len(arg) == 3 and arg.startswith('-o'):
                code=arg[2]
                if code not in SHORT_OUTPUT:
                    st.stderr_pre.append(f"nmap(-o{code}): unknown output format\n")
                    st.fatal=True; st.fatal_no_libpcap=True; i+=1; continue
                if i+1 >= len(args) or args[i+1].startswith('--'):
                    st.stderr_pre.append("missing output filename\n")
                    st.fatal=True; st.fatal_no_libpcap=True; i+=1; continue
                st.output_filename=args[i+1]; st.output_format=SHORT_OUTPUT[code]; i+=2; continue
            if arg.startswith('-o'):
                st.stderr_pre.append("missing output filename\n")
                st.fatal=True; st.fatal_no_libpcap=True; i+=1; continue
            # Unknown single dash
            name=arg[1:]
            st.stderr_pre.append(f"FAIL: unknown option: --{name}\n [hint] try \"--help\"\n [hint] ...or, to list nmap-compatible options, try \"--nmap\"\n")
            st.fatal=True; st.fatal_no_libpcap=True; i+=1; continue
        # Positional argument: target range(s), unless readscan wants a filename
        if st.readscan and st.readscan_file is None:
            st.readscan_file=arg; i+=1; continue
        # Try range. If token includes commas, each must be IP-like.
        bad_unknown=False
        for part in arg.split(','):
            token=part.strip()
            r=parse_one_range(token)
            if r is None:
                # Numeric-looking invalids are reported as bad IP; names are unknown parameters.
                if token and (token[0].isdigit() or ':' in token or '/' in token):
                    st.stderr_pre.append(f"ERROR: bad IP address/range: {token}\n")
                else:
                    st.stderr_pre.append(f"FAIL: unknown command-line parameter \"{token}\"\n [hint] did you want \"--{token}\"?\n")
                    st.fatal=True; st.fatal_no_libpcap=True; bad_unknown=True
                    break
            else:
                st.ranges.append(r)
        i+=1
    if st.send_eth_msg:
        st.stderr_pre.insert(0, "nmap(send-eth): unnecessary, we always do --send-eth\n")
    return st


def validate_large_scan(st: State) -> bool:
    port_count = sum(len(v) for v in st.ports.values())
    if port_count == 0:
        return True
    ranges = subtract_ranges(st.ranges, st.excludes)
    total = 0
    for ver,a,b in ranges:
        total += (b-a+1) * port_count
    if total and total.bit_length() > 63:
        st.stderr_pre.append(f"[-] FAIL: scan range too large, max is 63-bits, requested is {total.bit_length()} bits\n    Hint: scan range is number of IP addresses times number of ports\n    Hint: IPv6 subnet must be at least /66 \n")
        st.fatal=True
        return False
    return True


def echo_output(st: State) -> str:
    ranges = subtract_ranges(st.ranges, st.excludes)
    lines=[]
    lines.append(f"seed = {st.seed}")
    lines.append(f"rate = {fmt_rate(st.rate)}")
    lines.append(f"shard = {st.shard[0]}/{st.shard[1]}")
    if st.offline: lines.append("offline = true")
    if st.banners: lines.append("banners = true")
    if st.rawudp: lines.append("rawudp = true")
    if st.pcap_payloads is not None: lines.append(f"pcap-payloads = {st.pcap_payloads}")
    if st.pcap_filename is not None: lines.append(f"pcap-filename = {st.pcap_filename}")
    if st.hello_timeout is not None: lines.append(f"hello-timeout = {st.hello_timeout}")
    if st.http_cookie is not None: lines.append(f"http-cookie = {st.http_cookie}")
    if st.http_header is not None: lines.append(f"http-header = {st.http_header}")
    if st.http_method is not None: lines.append(f"http-method = {st.http_method}")
    if st.http_payload is not None: lines.append(f"http-payload = {st.http_payload}")
    if st.http_url is not None: lines.append(f"http-url = {st.http_url}")
    if st.http_user_agent is not None: lines.append(f"http-user-agent = {st.http_user_agent}")
    if st.http_host is not None: lines.append(f"http-host = {st.http_host}")
    for idx,s in enumerate(st.hello_strings):
        lines.append(f"hello-string[{idx}] = {s}")
    # Capture/nocapture display is duplicated by the original echo path.
    capblock=[]
    if st.nocapture_add:
        for x in sorted(st.nocapture_add):
            capblock.append(f"nocapture = {x}")
    capblock.append("nocapture = servername")
    for x in sorted(st.capture_add):
        if x:
            capblock.append(f"capture = {x}")
    lines.extend(capblock)
    lines.extend(capblock)
    lines.append("")
    output_lines=[]
    if st.output_append: output_lines.append("output-append = true")
    if st.output_filename is not None: output_lines.append(f"output-filename = {st.output_filename}")
    if st.output_format is not None: output_lines.append(f"output-format = {st.output_format}")
    if st.rotate is not None: output_lines.append(f"rotate = {st.rotate}")
    if st.rotate_dir is not None: output_lines.append(f"rotate-dir = {st.rotate_dir}")
    if output_lines:
        lines.extend(output_lines)
        lines.append("")
    else:
        lines.append("")
    adapter_lines=[]
    if st.adapter_echo is not None: adapter_lines.append(f"adapter = {st.adapter_echo}")
    if st.adapter_ip is not None: adapter_lines.append(f"adapter-ip = {st.adapter_ip}")
    if st.adapter_mac is not None: adapter_lines.append(f"adapter-mac = {st.adapter_mac}")
    if st.adapter_port is not None: adapter_lines.append(f"adapter-port = {st.adapter_port}")
    if st.router_ip is not None: adapter_lines.append(f"router-ip = {st.router_ip}")
    if st.router_mac_ipv4 is not None: adapter_lines.append(f"router-mac-ipv4 = {st.router_mac_ipv4}")
    if st.router_mac_ipv6 is not None: adapter_lines.append(f"router-mac-ipv6 = {st.router_mac_ipv6}")
    lines.extend(adapter_lines)
    lines.append("# TARGET SELECTION (IP, PORTS, EXCLUDES)")
    lines.append(f"ports = {fmt_ports(st)}")
    for r in ranges:
        lines.append(f"range = {range_to_text(r)}")
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def handle_readscan(st: State) -> int:
    # Echo has priority and never attempts to read the scan file.
    if st.echo:
        validate_large_scan(st)
        for s in st.stderr_pre: eprint(s)
        eprint(libpcap_message(st))
        sys.stdout.write(echo_output(st))
        return 0 if not st.fatal else 1
    for s in st.stderr_pre: eprint(s)
    eprint(libpcap_message(st))
    fn=st.readscan_file
    if fn is None:
        eprint("[-] FAIL: --readscan\n[-] (null): Bad address\n")
        return 0
    try:
        data=open(fn,'rb').read()
    except OSError as e:
        eprint(f"[-] FAIL: --readscan\n[-] {fn}: {e.strerror}\n")
        return 0
    eprint(f"[+] --readscan {fn}\n")
    # The bundled PCAP payload assets are not masscan binary result files.
    is_pcap = len(data) >= 24 and data[:4] in (b'\xd4\xc3\xb2\xa1', b'\xa1\xb2\xc3\xd4') and len(data) > 40
    if is_pcap:
        eprint(f"[-] {fn}: unknown file format (expeced \"masscan/1.1\")\n")
    else:
        # Original reports Success at EOF even for empty/truncated streams.
        eprint(f"[-] {fn}: Success\n")
        if st.output_filename and st.output_filename != '-':
            try:
                mode='ab' if st.output_append else 'wb'
                open(st.output_filename,mode).close()
            except OSError:
                pass
    return 0


def main(argv: List[str]) -> int:
    st=parse_args(argv)
    # Immediate informational exits
    if st.helpflag:
        sys.stdout.write(HELP if '--help' in argv else USAGE)
        return 1
    if st.nmapflag:
        sys.stdout.write(NMAP)
        return 1
    if st.versionflag:
        sys.stdout.write(VERSION)
        return 1
    # Fatal parse/config errors that occur before libpcap loading.
    if st.fatal and st.fatal_no_libpcap:
        for s in st.stderr_pre: eprint(s)
        if st.usage_needed:
            sys.stdout.write(USAGE)
        return 1
    if st.readscan:
        return handle_readscan(st)
    if st.iflist:
        for s in st.stderr_pre: eprint(s)
        eprint(libpcap_message(st))
        eprint("libpcap not loaded\n")
        return 0
    if st.selftest:
        for s in st.stderr_pre: eprint(s)
        eprint(libpcap_message(st))
        eprint("regression test: success!\n")
        return 0
    # Large scan validation applies even under --echo.
    if st.echo:
        validate_large_scan(st)
        for s in st.stderr_pre: eprint(s)
        eprint(libpcap_message(st))
        if st.fatal:
            return 1
        sys.stdout.write(echo_output(st))
        return 0
    # Non-echo normal path: load pcap, then usage/validation/scan failures.
    ports_empty = sum(len(v) for v in st.ports.values()) == 0
    ranges = subtract_ranges(st.ranges, st.excludes)
    ranges_empty = len(ranges) == 0
    # Print usage when nothing meaningful was specified or a parameter was empty.
    need_usage = st.usage_needed or (ports_empty and ranges_empty)
    if need_usage:
        sys.stdout.write(USAGE)
    for s in st.stderr_pre: eprint(s)
    eprint(libpcap_message(st))
    if need_usage:
        return 1
    if ports_empty:
        eprint('FAIL: no ports were specified\n [hint] try something like "-p80,8000-9000"\n [hint] try something like "--ports 0-65535"\n')
        return 1
    if ranges_empty:
        eprint('FAIL: target IP address list empty\n [hint] try something like "--range 10.0.0.0/8"\n [hint] try something like "--range 192.168.0.100-192.168.0.200"\n')
        return 1
    if st.offline:
        eprint("[-] FAILED: bad packet template\n")
        return 1
    eprint(f"FAIL:{st.adapter}: can't open adapter: libpcap not loaded\n[-] if:{st.adapter}:init: failed\n")
    return 1

if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

def eprint(s: str):
